options.text: Sir Edward Burnett Tylor
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Father of British Social Anthropology.

options.text: Sir James George Frazer
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Sir James George Frazer'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A. R. Radcliffe-Brown'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Max Gluckman
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Max Gluckman'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
E. B. Tylor was appointed the first academic professor of anthropology at Oxford University and penned the classic definition of culture in 1871.

chapter: Primate Taxonomy and Comparative Anatomy
questionText: Which living African great apes habitually practice 'Knuckle-Walking' quadrupedal locomotion on the ground?

options.text: Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) and Gorilla (Gorilla gorilla)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Knuckle-Walking in Great Apes.

options.text: Gibbon and Siamang
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Gibbon and Siamang'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Orangutan exclusively
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Orangutan exclusively'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Baboons and Colobus monkeys
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Baboons and Colobus monkeys'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Chimpanzees and gorillas walk terrestrially by bearing weight on the dorsal surfaces of the middle phalanges of their flexed fingers.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Early Hominid Evolution and Australopithecines
questionText: Ardipithecus ramidus ('Ardi', 4.4 Ma, Ethiopia) surprised paleoanthropologists because its postcranial skeleton exhibited:

options.text: Obligate high-speed bipedal sprinting
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Obligate high-speed bipedal sprinting'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Knuckle-walking identical to chimpanzees
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Knuckle-walking identical to chimpanzees'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Purely aquatic swimming adaptations
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Purely aquatic swimming adaptations'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Facultative bipedalism on the ground, combined with an abductable opposable grasping big toe for arboreal quadrumanous climbing
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Ardipithecus ramidus Locomotion.

detailedSolution:
Ardi proved that early hominins did not evolve from a knuckle-walking ancestor; she walked bipedally on ground while retaining an arboreal grasping big toe.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Evolution of Genus Homo: Homo habilis and Homo erectus
questionText: In Paleolithic archaeology, the 'Movius Line' formulated by Hallam Movius marks a theoretical geographic boundary separating:

options.text: Areas with Neanderthals from areas with Cro-Magnons
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Areas with Neanderthals from areas with Cro-Magnons'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Glaciated northern Europe from the Mediterranean
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Glaciated northern Europe from the Mediterranean'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Acheulean bifacial handaxe cultures of Africa, Europe, and Western Asia from the chopper-chopping non-biface cultures of East and Southeast Asia
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Movius Line Geographical Boundary.

options.text: Areas with iron from areas with bronze
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Areas with iron from areas with bronze'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
The Movius Line runs across northern India; west of the line rich Acheulean bifaces dominate, while east of it chopper-chopping traditions persisted.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Neanderthals and Anatomically Modern Homo sapiens
topic: Out of Africa (Recent African Origin) Model
questionText: The 'Out of Africa' (Recent African Origin / Replacement) model of modern human origins posits that:

options.text: Humans evolved independently from apes in 10 different continents simultaneously
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Humans evolved independently from apes in 10 different continents simultaneously'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Anatomically modern Homo sapiens evolved exclusively in Africa ~200,000–300,000 years ago, dispersing globally and replacing archaic Eurasian populations
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Out of Africa (Recent African Origin) Model.

options.text: Humans evolved in Australia 5 million years ago
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Humans evolved in Australia 5 million years ago'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Neanderthals gave birth to modern humans in Germany
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Neanderthals gave birth to modern humans in Germany'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Mitochondrial Eve and fossil discoveries confirm modern humans arose in Africa ~300 ka and expanded out ~60 ka, largely replacing archaic hominins.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Human Genetics and Mendelian Inheritance in Man
questionText: In human genetic pedigree charts, which feature definitively indicates an Autosomal Dominant mode of inheritance?

options.text: The trait appears exclusively in males and never in females
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The trait appears exclusively in males and never in females'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: The trait appears in every generation without skipping, and every affected child has at least one affected parent
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Pedigree Analysis: Autosomal Dominant Criteria.

options.text: The trait skips 10 generations continuously
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The trait skips 10 generations continuously'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Both parents must be completely disease-free
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Both parents must be completely disease-free'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Autosomal dominant traits display vertical transmission: an affected person has an affected parent, affecting both sexes equally, with 50% transmission risk.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Genetic Polymorphisms and Inborn Errors of Metabolism
questionText: The classic, unmistakable diagnostic clinical sign of Alcaptonuria in infants and adults is:

options.text: Urine that glows bright green under sunlight
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Urine that glows bright green under sunlight'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Urine smelling of ripe strawberries
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Urine smelling of ripe strawberries'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Zero urine production forever
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Zero urine production forever'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Urine that turns dark black upon standing or exposure to alkaline air, accompanied by dark pigmentation of cartilage (Ochronosis)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Alcaptonuria Diagnostic Sign.

detailedSolution:
Homogentisic acid accumulates and is excreted in urine, oxidizing into a dark melanin-like polymer upon atmospheric exposure, causing black urine.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Dermatoglyphics and Anthropometric Indices
topic: Simian Crease Single Palmar Transverse Flexion
questionText: A single, continuous, transverse horizontal flexion crease running completely across the palm ('Simian Crease') is found with high frequency in individuals with:

options.text: Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21) and fetal alcohol syndrome
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Simian Crease Single Palmar Transverse Flexion.

options.text: Olympic marathon runners exclusively
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Olympic marathon runners exclusively'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Individuals with blood group O
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Individuals with blood group O'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: All normal chimpanzees only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'All normal chimpanzees only'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
A single transverse palmar crease (fusion of proximal and distal transverse creases) occurs in ~1% of normal humans but >50% of Down syndrome individuals.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Human Variation and Biological Concept of Race
questionText: Gloger's Ecogeographical Rule states that within a warm-blooded mammalian species:

options.text: Populations inhabiting warm, humid equatorial zones evolve darker melanin pigmentation than populations residing in cold, arid high-latitude regions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Gloger's Ecogeographical Rule.

options.text: Animals in cold regions grow longer tails
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Animals in cold regions grow longer tails'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Animals in hot regions grow thick fur coats
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Animals in hot regions grow thick fur coats'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Animals in dark caves turn green
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Animals in dark caves turn green'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Gloger's rule reflects natural selection: heavy eumelanin protects tropical populations against intense solar ultraviolet radiation and microbial skin decay.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Ecological Anthropology and Environmental Adaptations
questionText: In high-latitude cloudy environments (e.g., northern Europe), natural selection favored light, depigmented skin because:

options.text: Light skin makes people run faster
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Light skin makes people run faster'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: UV-B radiation must penetrate the epidermis to photochemically synthesize 7-dehydrocholesterol into Vitamin D3, preventing pelvic deformity and rickets
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Rickets and Vitamin D Synthesis.

options.text: Light skin stops frostbite completely
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Light skin stops frostbite completely'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Light skin needs no food
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Light skin needs no food'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Melanin blocks UV-B; in northern regions with low solar UV, dark skin causes Vitamin D deficiency and pelvic rickets, causing fatal obstructed labor in females.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Concept of Culture and Society
questionText: Which universal attribute of human culture ensures that societies can adjust to environmental challenges, demographic pressures, and historical changes?

options.text: Culture is rigid, immutable, and permanently frozen from prehistoric times
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Culture is rigid, immutable, and permanently frozen from prehistoric times'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Culture exists only in physical genes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Culture exists only in physical genes'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Culture changes only through divine intervention
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Culture changes only through divine intervention'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Culture is dynamic and adaptive, continually modifying beliefs and technologies over time
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Dynamic Nature of Culture.

detailedSolution:
Culture is an adaptive mechanism that constantly changes, innovates, and borrows new elements to cope with evolving ecological and historical conditions.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Marriage: Forms, Rules and Tribal Mate Acquisition
topic: Bride Price Significance in Tribal Marriage
questionText: Anthropologists emphasize that 'Bride Price' (or bridewealth) paid by the groom's kin to the bride's kin functions primarily to:

options.text: Compensate the bride's family for the loss of her economic labor and reproductive capacity, legitimizing children in the groom's lineage
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Bride Price Significance in Tribal Marriage.

options.text: Purchase the woman as a private chattel slave with no social rights
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Purchase the woman as a private chattel slave with no social rights'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Pay for the bride's university tuition fees
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Pay for the bride's university tuition fees'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Bribe local police officials
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Bribe local police officials'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Bride price is not a purchase of a slave; it is a socially recognized transfer of wealth compensating the bride's lineage for her economic and reproductive loss.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Family: Types, Functions and Matrilineal Systems
questionText: In anthropological classification, what is the core structural difference between a 'Conjugal Family' and a 'Consanguineal Family'?

options.text: A conjugal family has no children, while a consanguineal family has 20 children
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A conjugal family has no children, while a consanguineal family has 20 children'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: A conjugal family lives in caves, while consanguineal lives in tents
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A conjugal family lives in caves, while consanguineal lives in tents'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: There is no difference
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'There is no difference'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: A conjugal family is centered on the marital bond between spouses, whereas a consanguineal family is centered on blood relations among descent kin
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Conjugal versus Consanguineal Family.

detailedSolution:
Conjugal families emphasize the affinal husband-wife partnership (e.g., nuclear family), whereas consanguineal families prioritize enduring lineage ties of blood.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Kinship Systems, Descent and Social Groups
questionText: In a 'Bilateral Descent' system (common in Western industrial societies and hunting-gatherer bands), an individual belongs to a 'Kindred', which is:

options.text: A permanent corporate group that owns land for 500 years
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A permanent corporate group that owns land for 500 years'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: An ego-centered, shifting network of bilateral relatives that has no permanent corporate existence and dissolves upon the death of the focal ego
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Bilateral Descent and Kindred.

options.text: A military battalion commanded by a hereditary colonel
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A military battalion commanded by a hereditary colonel'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: A group composed exclusively of males
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A group composed exclusively of males'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Unlike unilineal descent groups, a kindred is ego-centered: except for full siblings, no two people share the identical kindred, and it ceases at the individual's death.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Kinship Terminology and Kinship Usages
questionText: What is the crucial analytical difference between 'Parallel Cousins' and 'Cross-Cousins'?

options.text: Parallel cousins live in parallel streets, while cross-cousins live on hilltops
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Parallel cousins live in parallel streets, while cross-cousins live on hilltops'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Parallel cousins are older, while cross-cousins are younger
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Parallel cousins are older, while cross-cousins are younger'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: There is no difference
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'There is no difference'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Parallel cousins are children of siblings of the same sex (FBC and MSC), while cross-cousins are children of siblings of opposite sex (FSC and MBC)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Cross-Cousin Distinction in Kinship Systems.

detailedSolution:
Parallel cousins stem from same-sex sibling links (FB, MS); cross-cousins stem from opposite-sex sibling links (FS, MB) and are often preferred marriage partners.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Economic Anthropology: Primitive Economy and Exchange
questionText: Economic anthropologist Karl Polanyi distinguished 'Special-Purpose Money' (found in primitive societies) from modern 'General-Purpose Money' because special-purpose money:

options.text: Is printed on solid 24-karat gold bars only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Is printed on solid 24-karat gold bars only'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Can buy any commodity anywhere on the globe without restriction
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Can buy any commodity anywhere on the globe without restriction'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Expires within 24 hours of being minted
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Expires within 24 hours of being minted'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Can be used only to acquire specific categories of goods or services (e.g., bridewealth or ceremonial status) and cannot purchase ordinary everyday items
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Special-Purpose vs General-Purpose Money.

detailedSolution:
Special-purpose money (e.g., Tiv brass rods for brides, Yap stone Rai) serves limited transactional spheres, unlike general-purpose money which functions as a universal medium.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Political Anthropology: Law, Order and Social Control
topic: Max Weber's Tripartite Typology of Authority
questionText: Sociologist Max Weber identified three pure types of legitimate authority: Traditional, Charismatic, and:

options.text: Anarchical Authority
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Anarchical Authority'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Feudal Feasting Authority
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Feudal Feasting Authority'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Supernatural Demonic Authority
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Supernatural Demonic Authority'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: Rational-Legal Authority (anchored in codified rules, impersonal statutes, and bureaucratic office)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Max Weber's Tripartite Typology of Authority.

detailedSolution:
Weber's classic triad of legitimate authority comprises Traditional (customs/heredity), Charismatic (personal grace/magnetism), and Rational-Legal (institutional rules).
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Anthropology of Religion, Magic and Witchcraft
questionText: Anthropologist Victor Turner expanded van Gennep's concept of the 'Liminal Stage', demonstrating that during liminality, initiates experience:

options.text: Intense hatred and permanent warfare against their age-mates
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Intense hatred and permanent warfare against their age-mates'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: 'Communitas'—an intense, unstructured, sacred bond of absolute equality, comradeship, and dissolution of social status distinctions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Victor Turner: Liminality and Communitas.

options.text: Complete loss of all memories forever
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Complete loss of all memories forever'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
In 'The Ritual Process', Turner showed that liminal initiates exist 'betwixt and between' established statuses, fostering Communitas—profound egalitarian brotherhood.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Social Stratification, Caste and Jajmani System
questionText: In the rural Jajmani system, what was the structural role of the 'Kamin' (also known as Praja)?

options.text: The supreme king who owned all the land in India
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The supreme king who owned all the land in India'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: The foreign British tax inspector
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The foreign British tax inspector'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: The money-lender who ran a commercial bank
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The money-lender who ran a commercial bank'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

options.text: The artisan or service provider (such as blacksmith, barber, potter, washerman) who rendered traditional services to the patron and received customary grain shares (faslana)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Jajman versus Kamin / Praja Distinction.

detailedSolution:
In Jajmani relations, the Jajman was the landowning patron (often a dominant caste like Rajput or Jat); the Kamin/Praja was the service-provider receiving seasonal grain.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Anthropological Theories and Fieldwork Methods
questionText: What is 'Participant Observation', the foundational methodological fieldwork technique established by Bronislaw Malinowski in the Trobriand Islands?

options.text: Sending postal questionnaires to local English-speaking police officers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Sending postal questionnaires to local English-speaking police officers'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Observing villagers through a telescope from a cruise ship
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Observing villagers through a telescope from a cruise ship'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Long-term immersion in the community, living as a native, learning the indigenous language, and observing daily life from the 'native's point of view'
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Participant Observation Methodology (Malinowski).

options.text: Interviewing tribal immigrants in London museums
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Interviewing tribal immigrants in London museums'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Malinowski revolutionized fieldwork: living immersed in the village for years, speaking the vernacular, and documenting the 'imponderabilia of actual life'.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Geological Framework: Pleistocene Glaciations and Pluvials
questionText: What underlying astronomical mechanism drives the periodic pacing of Pleistocene glacial and interglacial cycles?

options.text: Periodic collisions of asteroids with the moon
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Periodic collisions of asteroids with the moon'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: The gravitational pull of passing comets every 10 years
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The gravitational pull of passing comets every 10 years'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Milankovitch Cycles: cyclical variations in Earth's orbital eccentricity, axial tilt (obliquity), and precession of equinoxes altering solar radiation distribution
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Milankovitch Astronomical Cycles.

options.text: Changes in the chemical salinity of seawater
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Changes in the chemical salinity of seawater'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Milutin Milankovitch showed that orbital eccentricity (100 ka), obliquity (41 ka), and precession (23 ka) drive cyclical glacial-interglacial climate pacings.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Dating Methods in Archaeological Anthropology
questionText: How did the development of 'Accelerator Mass Spectrometry' (AMS) revolutionize radiocarbon dating in modern archaeology?

options.text: It completely eliminated the need for computers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'It completely eliminated the need for computers'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: It allows dating of metallic gold coins and iron swords
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'It allows dating of metallic gold coins and iron swords'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: It counts individual Carbon-14 atoms directly rather than waiting for radioactive beta decays, requiring minuscule sample sizes (milligrams of charcoal or tiny bone fragments)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (AMS) Radiocarbon.

options.text: It increased the half-life of C-14 to 10 million years
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'It increased the half-life of C-14 to 10 million years'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
AMS requires samples 1,000 times smaller than conventional decay-counting (e.g., a single grain of burnt rice or speck of cave paint), preserving precious artifacts.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Paleolithic Technology: Flaking Techniques and Tool Typology
questionText: Stone Age knappers universally sought raw materials like flint, chert, obsidian, chalcedony, and fine-grained quartzite because these rocks exhibit:

options.text: Granular cleavage that shatters into square sugar-cube bricks
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Granular cleavage that shatters into square sugar-cube bricks'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Conchoidal Fracture: breaking along smooth, curved, shell-like surfaces that produce predictable, razor-sharp cutting edges upon impact
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Conchoidal Fracture Property.

options.text: Extreme flexibility that bends like rubber without breaking
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Extreme flexibility that bends like rubber without breaking'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Magnetic attraction that sticks to tree trunks
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Magnetic attraction that sticks to tree trunks'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Conchoidal fracture (typical of amorphous or cryptocrystalline silicates) allows shock waves to radiate predictably, enabling knappers to control flake geometry.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Lower Paleolithic Cultures: Oldowan, Acheulean and Soan Traditions
questionText: In early Indian prehistoric literature, the rich Acheulean bifacial handaxe and cleaver complex of Peninsular India was historically termed the:

options.text: Calcutta Industry
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Calcutta Industry'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Bombay Industry

options.text: Madrasian Industry (after Robert Bruce Foote's initial discoveries near Madras)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Madrasian Industry Nomenclature.

detailedSolution:
The Acheulean biface tradition in India was dubbed the 'Madrasian Industry' following Foote's pioneering discoveries in Attirampakkam and Pallavaram in the Madras region.
Hence, Option D is correct.

chapter: Middle Paleolithic Cultures: Mousterian and Levallois Technologies
questionText: In Middle Paleolithic Mousterian typology, what is 'Quina Retouch' (scalar retouch)?

options.text: Drilling circular holes through stone axes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Drilling circular holes through stone axes'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Polishing stone with sand and water
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Polishing stone with sand and water'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Steep, stepped, overlapping scalar flaking applied to the edges of thick scrapers, resembling fish scales
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Quina Retouch Characteristic.

options.text: Melting stone edges with fire
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Melting stone edges with fire'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Quina retouch features heavy, stepped, overlapping scalar flake scars on thick side-scrapers (racloirs), typical of the Charentian Mousterian facies.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Upper Paleolithic Cultures: Blade and Bone Technologies
questionText: What diagnostic organic artifact type characterizes the Upper Paleolithic Magdalenian culture, showing the intensive exploitation of riverine salmon and coastal seals?

options.text: Iron fishhooks with nylon monofilament lines
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Iron fishhooks with nylon monofilament lines'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Plastic fishing nets
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Plastic fishing nets'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Uniserial and Biserial barbed harpoons carved out of reindeer antler and mammoth bone
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Magdalenian Barbed Harpoons.

options.text: Wooden fishing rods equipped with metal reels
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Wooden fishing rods equipped with metal reels'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Magdalenian harpoons feature rows of sharp barbs (uniserial on one side, biserial on both) on antler rods, detachable from spear shafts for hunting fish and seals.

chapter: Evolution of Genus Homo: Homo habilis and Homo erectus
topic: Rising Star Cave Locality and Team Leader
questionText:
Read the following case study on the Discovery of Homo naledi in the Rising Star Cave System, and answer the questions that follow:

In 2013, recreational cavers discovered an unprecedented treasure trove of hominin fossils deep within the Rising Star cave system in the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage site near Johannesburg, South Africa. Led by paleoanthropologist Lee Berger of the University of the Witwatersrand, a team of underground speleological excavators (the 'underground astronauts') navigated the treacherous Superman's Crawl and a sheer 12-meter vertical chute known as the Chute to access the pitch-black Dinaledi Chamber. Over 1,550 fossil specimens representing at least 15 individuals were recovered from the cave floor. In 2015, Berger and his colleagues announced a new species: Homo naledi ('naledi' meaning 'star' in the local Sotho language). Homo naledi presents an astonishing mosaic anatomy: an ape-sized cranial capacity (465 to 560 cc), small body stature (approx. 145 cm), and curved australopith-like phalanges, coupled with modern human-like delicate cranial vault shape, small dentition, human-like wrists and palms suited for precision tool handling, and fully bipedal feet. Direct luminescence (OSL), electron spin resonance (ESR), and uranium-series dating unexpectedly established that Homo naledi lived between 335,000 and 236,000 years ago (Late Middle Pleistocene)—contemporaneously with the emergence of early Homo sapiens in Africa. Because the remote Dinaledi Chamber contained virtually no non-hominin animal bones or carnivore tooth marks, Berger proposed that Homo naledi intentionally navigated dark subterranean cave passages with torches to practice deliberate body disposal / mortuary caching.

Question: Who led the archaeological expedition that discovered the extraordinary Homo naledi fossil assemblage in the Rising Star cave system in South Africa?

options.text: Donald Johanson
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Donald Johanson'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Lee Berger
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately analyzes case evidence on Rising Star Cave Locality and Team Leader.

options.text: Raymond Dart
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Raymond Dart'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Mary Leakey
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Mary Leakey'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Lee Berger led the team from the University of the Witwatersrand that excavated the Rising Star cave system in 2013–2014.
Hence, Option B is correct.

Read the following excerpt on Marshall Sahlins and 'The Original Affluent Society', and answer the questions that follow:

In his 1972 classic 'Stone Age Economics', American economic anthropologist Marshall Sahlins overturned centuries of Western economic dogma by characterizing hunter-gatherers as 'The Original Affluent Society'. Classical Western economics (grounded in Adam Smith and formalist theory) assumes that human wants are infinite while resources are scarce, portraying primitive foragers as impoverished wretches engaged in a desperate, round-the-clock struggle against starvation. Drawing upon Richard B. Lee's empirical quantitative fieldwork among the Dobe !Kung San (Bushmen) of the Kalahari Desert and James Woodburn's studies of the Hadza of Tanzania, Sahlins demonstrated that foragers had remarkably plentiful lives. Adult !Kung foragers worked an average of only 3 to 5 hours per day (roughly 15 to 20 hours per week) to secure a nutritionally adequate diet of mongongo nuts, wild plants, and game, leaving abundant leisure time for storytelling, dance, visiting kin, and sleep. Sahlins argued that affluence can be attained in two ways: the 'Galbraithean capitalist road' of producing much to satisfy infinite wants, or the 'Zen road to affluence' of desiring little, where material wants are easily satisfied with simple technology, freeing man from the tyranny of scarcity.

Question: Which economic anthropologist coined the famous concept of 'The Original Affluent Society' in 'Stone Age Economics' (1972)?

options.text: Karl Polanyi
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Karl Polanyi'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Bronislaw Malinowski
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Bronislaw Malinowski'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Marshall Sahlins
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately analyzes case evidence on Originator of 'Original Affluent Society'.

options.text: George Dalton
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'George Dalton'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Marshall Sahlins formulated 'The Original Affluent Society' in 1972, refuting the myth of impoverished hunter-gatherers.
Hence, Option C is correct.
